reason: No existing skill covers proving a module-table, store-version or upgrade-path change on planted stores with old and new code side by side. The episode built exactly that proof by hand (HEAD copy vs working tree, planted version 14, conflict via retype) and hit several pitfalls worth keeping at the class level.

Ticket 13b34894 showed the store comparison missed CHECK, foreign key, unique/partial index and collation differences, and that a constraint change without a version raise slipped through; the worker also hit the sqlite_autoindex naming crash. This skill is the one the worker was running under and it only covers columns and index lists.
The description missed the trigger a user or agent hits when a live store is upgraded underneath running processes: the error text "schema version" is what surfaces, not the word "schema change".

A peer agent raised the live store to schema 22 while the web GUI, MCP server and runners still ran code that reads only 21, so their writes were refused. The skill proves changes on planted copies but says nothing about the live rollout or about processes that were started before the bump.

The existing rule was correct but did not reach the worker: the ticket said copy-first and the agent migrated live anyway, leaving running processes unable to write. The skill should say what to do when a worker breaks the rule.

The layout-22 upgrade passed schema proofs but created role-less elements (code, code.store, three in another project) that the map drew as parents of everything below them. The rule is to compare created rows, not only schema.

On 2026-10-15 the live memory store was at version 7 while the agent's own MCP server still ran pre-commit code; memory_create_entities refused with a version error. The skill says restart but not what to do when the agent cannot restart; the CLI fallback and the report duty were improvised.

After the layout 21 to 22 bump a system agent's runner logged every NewerStore and kept running for 50 minutes. The store-change skill tells you to restart old processes but says nothing about proving that a surviving process reacts to the refusal; a change that only checks schema would have passed with the runner still dead.

The episode used a copy-first upgrade with old-code compatibility proof for memory's version bump. That step is a reusable part of store-change proof and is not yet in the skill, which only covers planted-copy comparison and running processes.
The dispatch index bump surfaced a reusable proof pattern for index-only version changes and a reversal statement the report must carry. The skill covers version bumps generally but not this case.
Absorbed into verify-change-proof as its store-and-schema subsection; the recipe moved to its references/store-change-proof.md.
